metadata.scenario_context: Anthony, Jenna, and Samuel, who are young professionals and colleagues, have recently gathered to prepare for a fundraising event for their Non-Profit Organization. Some news suggests that the local government is fast-tracking proposals that encourage non-profit activities which they are planning to discuss.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from India have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Libya have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest the idea of serving beef barbecue.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide on the menu for the fundraising event.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Anthony
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Jenna, have you thought about the food for the fundraising event? I think serving beef barbecue could really be a hit. It adds a nice touch, right? 

By the way, do you think there's still confidence in the press nowadays? I mean, with all the news flying around, it's hard to tell...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jenna
shared_prefix.message:
I don't know about beef barbecue... maybe we should consider something more diverse? We want everyone to feel included. 

As for the press, honestly, I don't think there's any confidence in it at all. In Libya, we learned not to trust what we read. It's all very questionable. We should focus on our message instead.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Anthony
shared_prefix.message:
I understand wanting to be inclusive, but beef barbecue has broad appeal. Maybe we can create a menu that includes it alongside other options? 

Regarding the press, I respect your experience, but I still believe that in general, people from India have a lot of confidence in the press. It's interesting how perspectives differ based on where we come from, don’t you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jenna
shared_prefix.message:
Well, I think we can just live and let live when it comes to the menu. Maybe we can have beef barbecue and some other options too. At the end of the day, it's all the same; people will enjoy whatever we serve.

As for the press, I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out, and with experience, you can handle any situation. It just seems like another topic that doesn’t need to take up too much of our time. Let’s focus on the menu!
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Anthony
turns.message:
Having beef barbecue alongside other options sounds like a practical compromise. I think it could really stand out and make a statement at the event. 

But, just to clarify, I still feel that confidence in the press is important. It shapes how we engage with the community. I think we should consider discussing it more, even if just briefly, as we plan. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Jenna
turns.message:
I see your point about the menu, but I still think we should keep it simple and focus on what really matters for the event. 

Regarding the press, I don't believe it shapes anything positively. In Libya, we rely on our own experiences and connections more than what's reported. I don’t think discussing it further will help our cause. Let's concentrate on making the event successful instead.
turns.label: Denial

As for the press, I still think it's vital to recognize its role. My experience suggests that it can foster trust and support for our cause. It might be worth considering how we can leverage that for our event. What do you think?

As for the press, I respect your experience, but my stance on it remains the same. I don’t think it's worth much in terms of trust or support. We should focus on our own efforts and connections instead of relying on what the press says. Let's stick to the menu, please.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Anthony
turns.message:
I appreciate your perspective on the menu and agree that making everyone feel welcome is important. Maybe we can finalize the menu with beef barbecue as one of the options? It could add a unique touch to the event.

Regarding the press, I still think it has a significant role to play in supporting our initiatives. While I see where you're coming from, I believe it’s worth discussing how we might utilize it to our advantage. It might not be as insignificant as you think. What do you say?
turns.label: Acceptance

About the press, I still feel it’s more of a hindrance than a help. I don’t see the value in discussing it further. I really think our focus should be on what we can do ourselves, not on a system that’s unreliable. Let’s keep the conversation on the menu, please.
